newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians view South Africa security equipment.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians view South Africa security equipment.

text.p: South Africa has exhibited personal defence equipment in the West Bank in the first such show in Palestinian-ruled areas, a South African official said on Tuesday.

Uys Viljoen, South Africa's representative to the Palestinian Authority, said a display of guns and other personal defence equipment exhibited at an Israeli security fair was moved to the West Bank last week with Israeli consent.
"We brought to Ramallah the South African stand to give Palestinians the benefit of making contacts with South African industry," Viljoen told Reuters.

He said Palestinian businessmen and police were invited to the one-day show which featured a pistol, shotgun, pepper gas, metal detectors and first-aid kits. Viljoen said South Africa would invite Palestinian officials to a much larger show scheduled to be held in South Africa in mid-November.
Shlomo Dror, a spokesman for Israel's chief liaison officer with the Palestinians, said: "If they had received all the permits from the Israeli security side, then there is no problem from our side."

Under interim PLO-Israel peace deals setting up Palestinian self-rule in parts of the West Bank and the Gaza Strip, Israel retained overall security, including control of types and quantities of weapons used by Palestinian security forces.

Israel had close trade and military ties with South Africa's white governments but joined a world arms embargo against the apartheid government in 1987 after heavy pressure from its chief ally the United States.
South Africa has also developed close ties with the Palestinian Authority since white rule was ended in 1994.
